deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Σ = (X, Σ) is a system of pseudolines, i.e. an arrangement of pseudolines in a projective plane X. S denotes its set of vertices (multiple points). P = PR(Σ) is the set of 'relative positions' of one additional pseudoline D with respect to Σ, up to isotopy preserving Σ. These are the combinatorial types of one-element extensions Σ' = Σ ∪ {D}, including non-generic ones where D passes through vertices of Σ. The page, dated 23.12.83, begins giving P a structure: a directed graph of 'specialisation' arrows, with a cyclic order on the arrows at each vertex.

(a) Specialisation arrows. An arrow is a pair (D, T), where T is a 'specialisation triangle' for D.
- D̃ is the 'revêtement des rives' of D: the circle of the two sides (banks) of D, a double cover of D, with the polygonal structure induced by Σ.
- T is an arc on D̃ whose edges are cut out by ν ≥ 1 lines D_1, …, D_ν of Σ. These lines meet in a single vertex s of Σ, of order exactly ν, so that s has order ν+1 once D is included.
- The triangle (s, r, t) contains no vertex of Σ other than s.
- The arc's own vertices (the crossings of D with the D_i) are not vertices of Σ.
In modern terms, T is a fan-shaped cell complex between D and an isolated vertex s, with nothing in between. Pushing D across this fan until it passes through s gives a new position D', the 'pseudo-specialisation of D above T'. Then D'∩S = (D∩S) ∪ {s}, so D' is strictly more special than D. The trivial arrangement is excluded and treated separately.

The map P̃ → P × P, (D, T) ↦ (source, target) = (D, D'), is claimed injective. The argument (end of the left page and top of the right page):
- From (D, D') one recovers s as the unique vertex of Σ lying on D' but not on D.
- Hence one recovers the ν+1 curves bounding T: D and the ν lines of Σ through s.
- None of the relevant cells of Σ' = Σ ∪ {D} is a digon; otherwise Σ would be trivial.
- So the extreme edges of T, those joining s to D, are unique, and the arc of D̃ concerned is determined.
Thus P̃ ⊂ P × P, and one gets a strict (loopless, no multiple edges) oriented graph Γ(Σ) with vertex set P and edge set P̃, oriented from generic to special.

Local structure at a vertex D.
- Sp_0(D) is the set of immediate specialisations, in bijection with the specialisation triangles of D.
- Gn_0(D) is the set of immediate generisations, in bijection with pairs (s, s̃): s ∈ D∩S, and s̃ one of the points of D̃ over s, i.e. a choice of side to which D is pushed off s.

The next page continues:
- Each element of Sp_0 gives an open arc of D̃, these arcs being disjoint.
- Each element of Gn_0 gives a point of D̃ outside those arcs.
- So Sp_0(D) ⊔ Gn_0(D) inherits a cyclic (polygonal) order. This is a rotation system on the edges at D, i.e. the data of a 2-cell embedding of Γ(Σ) in a surface.
- He wants each such cycle to have at least three elements. When card(D∩S) ≥ 2 this is automatic. For stable D (no vertex of Σ on D) he uses that D is adjacent to at least 3 triangles of Σ' (Levi's theorem), each lying in a unique specialisation triangle. The semi-stable case (exactly one vertex on D) is handled separately.

Purpose. Grothendieck is evidently building a combinatorial cell structure (a map / polygonal complex, probably a 2-sphere) on the space of relative positions of a pseudoline. This is the rank-3 'extension space' of an oriented matroid, with specialisation order given by incidence with vertices.
errors: Counting inconsistency in the definition of T: the text speaks of 'ν+1 sommets' of the arc and of a point s 'd'ordre exactement ν+1', while later the ν+1 curves are D plus the ν lines of Σ through s. So s has order ν in Σ (ν+1 in Σ∪{D'}), and the arc carries ν crossing points of D. The definition as written mixes these counts; the intended meaning is clear but the indexing wobbles.

The injectivity argument is only sketched ('on voit de même…'). The step excluding digons, and showing that the extreme edges of T and hence the whole arc are recoverable from (D, D'), relies on the nontriviality of Σ and is not fully written. It is plausible, but a gap.
Notation drift: Gn_0(D) on this page is apparently called Cerc_0(D) on the next page.

The claim that every vertex has at least 3 incident arrows is marked 'je crois'. The stable case uses Levi's theorem (each pseudoline of a nontrivial projective arrangement is adjacent to at least 3 triangles), which is correct. The semi-stable case is left unfinished on the following page.

ideas.what: Set PR(Σ) of relative positions of a new pseudoline with respect to an arrangement, including degenerate positions through vertices
ideas.modern_name: Extension space / poset of single-element extensions of a rank-3 oriented matroid (localizations, cocircuit signatures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Las Vergnas (single-element extensions, 1978); Sturmfels–Ziegler, 'Extension spaces of oriented matroids' (1993); Mnëv–Richter-Gebert (1993)

ideas.what: Specialisation/generisation order on positions, with arrows given by pushing D across an empty fan ('specialisation triangle') onto a vertex s
ideas.modern_name: Covering relations in the face poset of the extension space; degenerate triangle flips / mutations through a vertex

ideas.what: Injectivity of P̃ → P×P, making the specialisation structure a strict oriented graph Γ(Σ)
ideas.modern_name: Hasse diagram (cover graph) of the extension poset

ideas.what: Cyclic (polygonal) order on Sp_0(D) ⊔ Gn_0(D) induced from the circle D̃ of the two banks of D, i.e. a rotation system at each vertex of Γ(Σ)
ideas.modern_name: 2-cell embedding / combinatorial map structure on the extension space (link of a vertex is a polygon)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in the Sturmfels–Ziegler result that rank-3 extension spaces are spherical (unsure of exact attribution)

ideas.what: Terminology 'stable' (D avoids all vertices) and 'semi-stable' (one vertex) positions, and scheme-theoretic 'specialisation/generisation' language
ideas.modern_name: Generic vs non-generic extensions; GIT-style and Zariski-specialisation vocabulary transplanted to combinatorics
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mumford (GIT terminology); Grothendieck (specialisation language in EGA)

ideas.what: Use of 'each pseudoline is adjacent to at least 3 triangles' to bound the degree of Γ(Σ)
ideas.modern_name: Levi's triangle theorem for pseudoline arrangements

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently sets up the rank-3 extension space of a pseudoline arrangement. He gives it a specialisation order, a strict directed graph, and a rotation system coming from the bank-circle D̃, clearly aiming at a polygonal surface structure. This anticipates the Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993) study of extension spaces and their sphericity in rank 3, about a decade earlier, and it is uncredited.
missed.quote: On trouve donc un graphe strict orienté … P comme ens. de sommets, P̃ comme ens. d'arêtes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority aside, his explicit local model may give a direct combinatorial route to the cell structure and sphericity of rank-3 extension spaces. In this model, each vertex D has a polygon formed by arcs of D̃ (specialisations) and points over vertices (generisations).

missed.claim: Lower bound ≥3 on the valence of every vertex of Γ(Σ): proven in the stable case via Levi's theorem, left incomplete in the semi-stable case on the next page.
missed.quote: Cet ens. a au moins trois éléments je crois.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the condition needed for the local polygons to be genuine 2-cells. It is a small, checkable lemma, but its completion would tie the notes to the known sphericity results.

deep.surprise_reason: The page develops, in Grothendieck's own vocabulary, what is now the extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid, with a rotation-system structure. That predates Sturmfels–Ziegler and is not recorded in the literature. But the mathematics itself is now standard, and the page is a preliminary setup with a sketchy injectivity proof.
transcription_corrections: 'le vers. des rives de D' should read 'le revêt. des rives de D': D̃ is the covering (circle) of the two banks of D.
'D_0 S = (D∩S) ∪ {s}' is in the image 'D'∩S = (D∩S) ∪ {s}', the vertex set on the specialised line D'.

'Sp_0(D) l'ens. de ses (immédiates) "successeurs" spécialisations': the inserted words are '(immédiates)' and probably 'successeurs', written above 'spécialisations'. A struck-through 'Gn_0(D)' follows.
Left margin word 'contre-rive' near the drawing is crossed out.
The specialisation triangle is described as 'ens. de ν ≥ 1 [arêtes] sur D̃ … formant un arc sur D̃'; the noun after 'ens. de' is unclear in the image.
